quantity: EIRP of the Arecibo planetary radar (S band), the benchmark the abstract and conclusions compare the limits with

adopted_source.reference: Sheikh S. Z., Huston M. J., Fan P., Wright J. T., Beatty T., Martini C., Kopparapu R., Frank A., 2025, AJ, 169, 118 (arXiv:2502.02614)
adopted_source.quote: Arecibo's characteristic EIRP at S-band is 20 TW (Ekers et al. 2002)
adopted_source.secondary: Ekers R. D., Cullers D. K., Billingham J., Scheffer L. K., 2002, SETI 2020 (SETI Press, Mountain View)

cross_checks.quote: an Arecibo Planetary Radar (EIRP=2.2 x 10^13 W) is detectable at 415 ly

cross_checks.reference: Enriquez J. E., et al., 2017, ApJ, 849, 104 (arXiv:1709.03491)
cross_checks.quote: L_AO is the EIRP of the Arecibo Planetary Radar at 10^13 W
cross_checks.note: an order-of-magnitude normalisation of the CWTFM (this paper's \FomAreciboEirp), not a measured EIRP; consistent to within its own rounding

transmitter_check: P_tx G = 1 MW x 10^(73/10) = 2.0e13 W (the radar's ~1 MW klystron output at 2.38 GHz into the 305 m dish's ~73 dBi gain); the 2.38 GHz frequency is the physical radar frequency, Sheikh et al. write '2.4 GHz'
note: The comparison is of EIRP only. The limits of this paper are isotropic-equivalent powers at 84-950 GHz; an Arecibo-sized dish at those frequencies is not a realisable transmitter, so the benchmark is not frequency-scaled (see numbers_v410.py / macromap ArecScaledW).
